summary: A satirical piece on government attempts to build a cybersecurity workforce pipeline, mocking bureaucratic buzzword use, failed training programs, botched hackathons, wasted budgets and a nationwide blackout. It argues, through humor, that neglecting cybersecurity workforce development in national policy leads to ongoing cyber incidents and farce.
one_line: A satirical take on governments' bungled efforts to develop a cybersecurity workforce, from useless workshops and hackathons to wasted budgets and a blackout.
key_facts: The article is satire and is dated as of Sept 21, 2023, describing governments scrambling to patch cyber defenses.
John Smith, a government official, led a 200-page National Cybersecurity Strategy and boasted "We're going to pipeline the heck out of our cyber workforce."
The pipeline is described as a pipedream with more holes than Swiss cheese.
Workshops, webinars and e-learning courses with names like "Cyber Hero 101" and "Bytes and Fights" had empty seats because RSVPs were mistaken for malware.
A nationwide blackout on Oct 5, 2023 occurred because the intern who knew how to reset the router took a personal day.
Cyber Agent X, a superhero-like recruitment figure, was portrayed by actor and part-time karaoke champion Chad Thunder.
Chad Thunder's first public speech as Cyber Agent X failed when he forgot his password and got locked out of his own presentation.
University cyber degree programs such as "The Art of Ethical Hacking" were taught by professors who thought Python was a snake and Java a place to get coffee, and students dropped out.
Government-sponsored hackathons became "face-palm-athons" when participants breached their own systems; a 13-year-old winner hacked the scoreboard to stay in the lead.
Government canteens meant to offer brain-boosting snacks ended up supplying sugary treats and caffeinated drinks 24/7.
Bureaucracy required triplicate forms, and budgets were lost to consultancy fees for gurus recommending things like "synergizing paradigms" and "quantum-encrypted blockchain AI ecosystems."
The article concludes that neglecting cybersecurity workforce development in national policy will keep producing incidents and material for satirical reporters.
